title: Design system contribution workflow, RFC staging, and graceful deprecation protocol
creator: Marco Chen
description: Create a single, pragmatic contribution workflow and review checklist for the Redwood Design System that covers tokens, primitives (buttons, inputs), layout components (tables, grids), and charts. The doc must include: a standard RFC staging template, an automated lint+CI gating checklist, author and reviewer roles, design & engineering sign-off path, semantic versioning guidance for tokens vs components, deprecation protocol with migration windows and consumer notification recommendations, and a tiny-migrations playbook for breaking changes. This ticket consolidates prior scattered notes into a living guideline used by Design, DX, and Engineering.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical CONTRIBUTING section is added to the design repo with step-by-step flow
An RFC template is published to Confluence with staging and review states
Automated CI checks (lint, token diff warnings, storybook build) are listed and integrated guidance provided
A deprecation policy is defined with minimum migration windows for tokens and components and templated consumer communication
Design and Eng sign-off matrix documented (roles and required approvals) and dogfooding checklist present
At least one mock deprecation runbook and a sample RFC demonstrating the flow exist with links
tasks: Draft contribution flow (author -> peer review -> design review -> eng review -> release)
Design RFC template: problem statement, compatibility impact, migration strategy, adopters list
Write review checklist for tokens (naming, token collisions, semantic mapping)
Write review checklist for components (accessibility, responsive states, visual QA, stories)
Define deprecation windows: tokens 60 days, minor components 90 days, major components 180 days (draft)
Add CI hooks to warn when token values change and require explicit rationale in RFC
Create communication templates (Slack, release notes, changelog) for deprecation notices
Publish docs to Confluence and add link from design system README
decisions: Adopt RFC-first requirement for any change touching public tokens or component API
Separate versioning rules: tokens follow 'token-semver' (value/intent), components follow semver with explicit breaking change markers
Minimum migration windows chosen (tokens 60d / minor components 90d / major components 180d) to balance agility and customer impact
Automated token-diff warnings will block merge until a linked RFC is present or reviewer overrides with documented reason
